correctness.rationale: For one vacancy, same-part jumps preserve the mover’s payoff. Cross-part color moves occur only along the alternating macrostate path A_i—B_i—A_(i−1) and use reversed exact pre/post fractions in the opposite direction, so every edge has at most one strict orientation. There are at most 2(b+1) macrostates, giving termination by 2b+1 moves and existence of a Nash state. For two vacancies, four exactly specified labeled jumps on K3,3 at peak 9/20 have strict exact rational payoff pairs and return to the identical configuration. Replayed 2,250 one-vacancy parameter instances and the cycle with exact arithmetic; enumeration alone does not prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: Full text of the main 2023 single-peaked jump paper separates ring-specific convergence and bipartite sufficient equilibrium existence from the present biclique-wide, all-peaks, color-heterogeneous FIP and explicit update bound. The diversity-seeking result assumes a particular monotone payoff and regularity and thus cannot cover the arbitrary-payoff result. Swap and ordinary Schelling results use different models. The explicit two-vacancy K3,3 labeled cycle is not implied by previously described path or ring cycle constructions. Prioritization risk from unidentified general fixed-composition improvement dynamics remains, but inspected sources do not dominate the claim.
residual_risks: An equivalent orientation argument may have appeared in specialized unpublished, unindexed or older potential-game work.
Other broad arbitrary-payoff potentiality theorems may cover complete bipartite one-vacancy dynamics without using Schelling terminology.

value.rationale: A complete bipartite graph is a natural two-community social network. The result guarantees termination of every improvement trajectory and an explicit short bound for all single-peaked peaks, even under arbitrary color-specific nonmonotone preferences and balanced populations. The companion repeated-jump cycle on a regular biclique shows a sharp qualitative change after adding a single vacant location. Such a global topology-plus-vacancy boundary goes beyond a routine Nash existence or parameter substitution.
